scope: All nine installed standard Embrace the Future videos, 37 minutes 33 seconds. Current local course references and source hashes identify the versions reviewed.
method: Sequentially decoded all nine sources; all frame counts match. Visually inspected 22 contact sheets sampled every six seconds and five closer sequence sheets around the selected shots. recommendation: Build three focused updates: a student improving an agent-made basketball reel, a recognizable data-center exterior, and a student actively building expertise. Preserve the other six videos and the recent repairs throughout the section.

opportunities.title: Show the student improving the finished reel
opportunities.cue: If an agent creates the TikTok clip and caption, you are responsible for reviewing it and making it better. Agents are good, but not perfect.
opportunities.current: A robot hand passes a pen to a human under “HUMAN OVERSIGHT REQUIRED.” It communicates responsibility abstractly, without showing the basketball example being evaluated.
opportunities.proposal: Return to the narrated basketball highlight reel. Show a high-school student reviewing the assembled clips on a laptop, then making a visible improvement to the selection or caption. Use a clear basketball frame, a simple edit timeline, and two matched screen states.
opportunities.benefit: Makes “reviewing it and making it better” an observable action. The learner sees what their judgment contributes after the agent has done the assembly.

1:55.28–1:58.38: on “reviewing it and making it better,” emphasize the selected clip and reveal a small edit to the reel or caption.
1:58.38–2:01.10: retain both the context and the improvement through “good, but not perfect,” then return to the existing Rogue Agents board.
opportunities.treatment: Photographic scene with deterministic screen content and restrained motion. Keep the student, clothing, camera, court footage and device geometry consistent. Choose the exact edit during the build so its benefit is visible without adding a new narrated story. This is the retained basketball evaluation example, not a universal permission gate. Do not restore the later review-button graphic or send/spend/submit/delete/post rule removed in v7.

opportunities.title: Show a data center, with the right physical cues
opportunities.cue: The scale varies by facility, but the mechanical process is consistent.
opportunities.current: A split drawing pairs server racks with an industrial complex featuring large cooling towers and power pylons. The exterior can read as a power station rather than a data center.
opportunities.proposal: Replace this brief cutaway with a realistic illustrative exterior of a warehouse-scale data center: low buildings, visible cooling equipment, and electrical service. Compose the facility clearly enough to recognize in four seconds.
opportunities.benefit: Connects the racks already shown inside to the kind of physical facility that houses them. Avoids conflating the computer facility with the power plant supplying it.
beats: 1:10.73–1:14.80: one clear facility view with a restrained push while the narrator qualifies that scale varies.
Return on the existing cut to the chat-to-data-center explanation at 1:14.80.
opportunities.treatment: One photographic-style illustration is sufficient. Use plausible ordinary cooling equipment, no landmark generating-station towers, no invented company/location, and no numerical scale claim. This is a generic teaching illustration, not documentary evidence of a named facility. The neighboring football-field/small-city comparison stays as it is.
opportunities.board: Preserve the canonical interior photograph, all three boards, neighbor-effect highlights, the chat diagram and closing sequence. Preserve v5’s example-specific calculation captions at about 0:10 and 3:02.
opportunities.success: The shot reads as a computing facility and does not suggest that the data center itself is a power plant.
opportunities.reference: Current canonical Inside a Data Center image for subject continuity; Learning Illustration Pass photographic setting treatment. Do not add a person simply to match a student-scene template.

opportunities.title: Make “build that expertise yourself” visible
opportunities.cue: Your only defense against this trap is relentless learning. You have to build that expertise yourself, making your time in school right now the greatest advantage you could possibly have.
opportunities.current: An empty desk drawing shows a book, papers, a lamp, and a blank monitor. It represents studying, but nobody is doing the learning.
opportunities.proposal: Show a high-school student working through a problem in their own notebook, comparing their attempt with course material, and revising the reasoning. Use the same student and desk across two matched states, with the work itself large enough to see.
opportunities.benefit: Turns the closing advice into deliberate practice. The scene shows how a learner starts building the knowledge needed to judge sophisticated work later.
beats: 5:10.53–5:13.86: show the learner making their own attempt as “relentless learning” is spoken.
5:13.86–5:20.37: on “build that expertise yourself,” show the same work being checked against course material and revised; hold through the reference to school.
Cut to the unchanged canonical close at frame 9611.
opportunities.treatment: Follow the approved Learn With AI study-scene continuity and Why Learn AI? revision reference. Use a simple, internally correct worked example selected during the build; render any essential marks separately. Avoid a generic typing pose, a new AI chat exchange, or a success badge. Two coherent states are enough for this ten-second interval.
opportunities.board: Preserve the preceding expertise-gap drawing, the existing source-checking photograph and strategic-human-value animation, every course board and highlight, and the final close. No change to the owner-approved narrative.
opportunities.success: The viewer sees the student doing intellectual work and improving their understanding, rather than merely being near study materials.
opportunities.reference: Learn With AI for matched study states; Why Learn AI? garden-project revision for visible hands-on learning and mature photographic composition.
